gen-dafont-nordic-gf-ruda: Ancient and blunt, with letters spaced like far-apart brush dabs. Ruda answers in a wire-thin monoline with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds, plain sans friendly where Nordic is tight and closed.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-saira: Weathered and weighty, Nordic is all one monoweight stroke. Saira, a plain sans with see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching toward the top line, gives the pair its strongest quality: closed against open.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sarpanch: Stonelike and ancient, Nordic keeps every opening pinched shut like a pressed leaf fold. Sarpanch, a plain sans with a clearly open e and compact ascenders, is the one that stays friendly over many lines, while Nordic hits hardest as a title.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-savate: Nordic brings a powerful, ancient feel, its monoweight strokes spaced like brush dabs set well apart on paper. Savate keeps the reading smooth, with open curves and sturdy hairlines.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk brings big open e and a shapes with tall bowls and terminals that never close in. Make Nordic small and its cramped, leaf-fold openings clog up, while Schibsted Grotesk stays inviting even at generous sizes.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sen: Tight, old, and forceful, Nordic is drawn with one monoweight stroke and brush-dab spacing. And Sen, a sans-serif built tall with curves that stop before turning inward, lets the page breathe right below it.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sintony: Sintony reads smoothly, with a chunky, tall midzone and no clogged curves in sight. Sintony only has low stroke modulation while Nordic has none at all, and that near-match in line is what holds the pair together.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans stands its lowercase tall, like cut acrylic stencil pieces, with rounded letters left clearly open at the side. Yet Nordic shares its lack of thick-and-thin modulation, so the pair's strongest quality is a single drawn line, one tight, one open.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sofia-sans-semi-con: Nordic's cramped, leaf-fold openings give it an ancient, powerful bite. But Sofia Sans Semi Condensed, with lowercase nearly matching its capitals and a big entrance into each curve, is the one built for steady text.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-sono: Sono reads with wide spacing and tall lowercase, each a left ajar. Nordic traces every stroke at one stylus width and stays closed up, so the two sit together like a carved stone beside an open window.
